concerns.text: The visual layout latent target is generated by rendering the *same* plain text into a synthetic image and then passing that image through a frozen visual encoder. Because the image is a deterministic function of the text, the latent is a deterministic function of the text as well. Training a DistilledModel to predict this latent from the original text and then claiming a statistically significant MSE improvement over a random‑vector baseline is tautological: any model that learns a deterministic mapping will necessarily outperform a random baseline, making the reported MSE gain true by definition rather than an empirical discovery.

The downstream evaluation compares an ‘augmented’ model (text embedding + predicted visual latent) against a text‑only baseline. Since the predicted latent is derived from the same text (via the deterministic rendering pipeline), it does not provide information independent of the text input. Consequently, any observed performance gain could be attributed to increased model capacity or over‑fitting rather than genuine additional layout knowledge. The plan’s ablation claim that Pearson r < 0.3 between predicted latent and text‑only embedding is unlikely given the deterministic relationship, indicating a flawed independence assumption in the validation.
